match.reason: The closest bank point, geo-land-biomes, describes what each land biome is like rather than the latitude bands where they sit, including deserts around 30 degrees, so it does not teach the same idea.

note:
A fresh check found these problems in this version. Fix each one, and keep everything that is right:
- Question a, wording: The distractor 'Mountains are always arranged in east to west lines' uses 'always', but the card only says mountains 'can' break up the bands. The absolute word marks it as wrong without testing the idea.
- Question a, other: The clue 'What two climate features decide a biome?' points straight at the only option that names two climate features, so a student can pick it without understanding why latitude matters.

rejected.title: Where the world's biomes are
card: A biome is set mainly by its temperature and rainfall. Both change with latitude, which is how far a place is north or south of the equator.
Because of this, biomes form rough bands that run east to west around the globe. Mountains and ocean currents can break up these bands.
Near the equator
it is hot and wet all year, so tropical rainforests grow there.
Further out
deserts are common around 30 degrees north and south, where rainfall is low. Tundra lies near the poles, where it is very cold.
rejected.remember: Temperature and rainfall change with latitude, so biomes form bands from the equator to the poles.

a.q: Why do biomes form bands by latitude?
opts: Temperature and rainfall change with latitude
Soil type is the same along each line of latitude
Animals move along lines of latitude to find food
Mountains are always arranged in east to west lines
a.why: Biomes depend mainly on temperature and rainfall, and both change with latitude. Soil and animals do not set the bands. Mountains can break the bands up rather than make them.
a.clue: What two climate features decide a biome?

b.q: Lena studies a world biome map. Which biome is she most likely to find at about 30 degrees south, and why?
opts: Desert, because rainfall is low at that latitude
Tundra, because it is very cold at that latitude
Tropical rainforest, because it is wet all year there
Desert, because it is very cold all year there
b.why: Deserts are common around 30 degrees north and south because rainfall there is low. Desert with the reason very cold is tempting, but cold is what makes tundra near the poles, not deserts at 30 degrees.
b.clue: Check both the biome and the reason the card gives for it.

wants.brief: A simple world map with latitude lines at the equator, 30 degrees north and south, and the poles. Horizontal bands are labelled: tundra near the poles, deserts around 30 degrees north and south, tropical rainforest along the equator.
wants.why: Seeing the bands on a map shows how biomes line up with latitude.
